overall: Atlanta is currently sitting at 91.4°F (running max) at 13:50 ET, with a positive velocity of +1.8°F/hr indicating continued warming, though the 30-minute velocity has flattened to 0.0°F/hr and acceleration is negative at -0.900°F/hr², signaling a decelerating warming trend. Broken cloud cover (BKN, 62% cloud fraction) is partially limiting solar insolation, and a Heat Advisory is in effect with heat index values potentially reaching 106°F across northeast Georgia — consistent with the high dewpoints (73.4°F) observed.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in significant disagreement: GFS is bullish at 98.3°F while ECMWF (94.4°F), HRRR (94.7°F), and NBM (93.6°F) cluster in the mid-90s; current observed temperatures are running well behind even the more conservative model solutions, requiring sustained or accelerating warming through the afternoon to bridge the gap. Peak timing is the critical wildcard — HRRR pegs peak at 18:00 ET (allowing ~4 more hours of heating), while GFS places it at 14:00 ET (nearly now), creating a 4-hour spread that fundamentally drives the uncertainty between a ~93°F and ~98°F outcome.
max_temp_prediction: With the current running max at 91.4°F, decelerating warming, and the dominant cluster of ECMWF/HRRR/NBM models centering near 94–95°F, the most likely peak is in the 94–96°F range, with 96–97°F (the top even bucket at 28.5% per D1_NOW, and further supported by the META model which heavily weights 96–99°F at ~82% combined) remaining a meaningful upside scenario if peak timing is delayed toward 16–18h ET. The 98-99°F GFS solution appears an outlier given current observed temperatures and the moderate cloud cover suppressing heating. Confidence is moderate — the active even-bucket market top of 96–97°F is plausible but requires the late-peak HRRR scenario to materialize.
